resolutions.reproduced: Yes, both halves, independently. (a) With `boilerplate_applied` reverted to the pre-merge `any("display_text" in i for i in items)` on the merged tree, the gate was fully green — invariant 58/58, fast 116/116 — and only `python3 -m src.sec10k.web.view` went red; that runner is in .github/workflows/ci.yml but in neither `## Gate` nor .githooks/pre-commit. resolutions.covered_by: evals/adversarial/ui-exclusion-note-trigger.json, extended: `input.blocks_modes: [false, true]` drives every fixture in BOTH view modes, and the oracle is a new `_chrome_inside_items(env)` — do any of the envelope's own boilerplate spans fall inside an item's span. Five fixtures x two modes = 10 runs per gate pass.
resolutions.oracle_choice: Deliberately NOT `strip_chrome(...) != raw`, which the finding offered as the obvious candidate: that is the expression `build_view` itself now uses, so a check built on it would re-run the implementation and agree with any window bug the implementation has — the argument `check_boilerplate_exclusion` already makes about its own oracle. `_chrome_inside_items` reads the envelope's spans and the item offsets and nothing else. It satisfies the stated acceptance (not `any("display_text" in i)`) and is strictly more independent.
